* [[NATO]] helicopters find the wreckage of a [[Kam Air Boeing 737 disaster|Kam Air Boeing 737]], an [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] passenger jet, in mountains east of [[Kabul]]; all 104 people that were on board are presumed dead. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=473996 (ABC News)]
* [[Bareilly]], [[India]]: More than 250 grams of weapons-grade [[uranium]] are found in possession of two people arrested for drug peddling in [[India]]. [http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/1012203.cms (Times of India)]
* [[List of Presidents of Togo|President]] [[Gnassingbé Eyadéma]] of [[Togo]] dies of a [[myocardial infarction|heart attack]] at the age of 68 and is succeeded by his son [[Faure Gnassingbé]]. [http://www.cnn.com/2005/WORLD/africa/02/05/togo.president.ap/index.html (CNN)]
* In the [[People's Republic of China]], The Tenth [[Shaanxi]] Provincial [[Shaanxi People's Congress|People's Congress]] votes in favour of Acting Governor [[Chen Deming]] to become the next [[Governor]] of Shaanxi. [http://www.people.com.cn/GB/paper464/14043/1252809.html (People's Daily)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} [https://web.archive.org/web/20051101112809/http://gb.chinabroadcast.cn/3821/2005/02/06/301@445416.htm (ChinaBroadcast)]
* In [[Malawi]], [[Heads of State of Malawi|President]] [[Bingu wa Mutharika]] quits the governing party, the [[United Democratic Front (Malawi)|United Democratic Front]], stating he is fed up of criticism of his anti-[[Political corruption|corruption]] campaign. The party had debated whether to expel him for alleged misconduct.
